My friend took her son to the children's psych ward on Friday. I want to say the boy is 12. Close to that. My friend is so swamped caring for her other boy, her job, etc, we haven't had time to talk about why he went in there. I know he has a history of anxiety, but nothing like this.

Does anyone have any experiences with something like this? Can anything good come of this?
Do you have any experience with children's psych wards?

Unfortunately I have experience with this and yes something good can come of it. Please be as supportive as possible this is likely the most difficult decision of her life and not something done lightly. Please do not second guess because no matter how close you may be to the family you likely have no idea just what they are dealing with and how overwhelming the struggle may be. She is likely questioning herself if it was the right thing to do especially if this is the first time.

If she needs to talk please listen. If she doesn't want to talk don't pressure her. Work may be the only place where she can temporarilly focus on something else and feel somewhat normal.

Feel free to pm me if you want to talk.

Thank you. I've been trying to be quiet and give her space. She talks to me sometimes, so I get a few details, but not about the core of the matter.

I had to take my ex to one once. He had completely disconnected from reality and was a danger to himself and others. They gave him meds to help him sleep and I think ultimately he did not resent me for taking him. But god, that place was terrible. The only good they did for my ex was to give him sleeping pills. They released him after a week and he was still not himself at that time, and there was no follow up. I really worry for my friend's son. She said he sounds "nervous." Christ.

And yes, it's one of the most difficult decisions of her life, so I don't want my worries to seep into the conversation. I just want to support her. She has extensive experience with mental health crises (herself and her friends), so I trust her judgement on this. I just posted this because I wanted to hear someone say it is possible for this to help, because I doubt that so much.

A psych hospital can be a frightening and overwhelming place but it does serve a purpose. It really is possible for this to be a help but a good support system must be in place when the child gets home. The support system is as much about the child as the rest of the family. Sometimes mom will need something as simple as a night out and know her child is safe. The child will need to feel loved and supported despite the issues that are being dealt with. A sibling may need an afternoon that is all about them so they can feel special and worthy of attention. Dad may need a few quiet hours to unwind and watch a game. Hospitalization can be beneficial but aftercare is also key and little things make a big difference.

It would break my heart to see the children in the hospital that had no such support system. There were times I wanted to bring them home with me and show them that someone cares. There were other times I was thankful for the situation I was dealing with because I could see how much worse things could be.

You sound like a good friend and coworker. The fact that you care is helpful. You are essentially a part of the support system. Even if you never meet the child just by being supportive of the mom really makes a positive difference in all of their lives.

I was fortunate to have a wonderful work environment. I never felt pressure to prioritize work over family. I was expected to care for my family first and foremost and only once they were safe would I come into the office. While in the office I felt normal and productive even a bit relaxed, the most challenging work problems were nothing in comparison. If I felt like opening up I was able to share as much or as little as I was comfortable. Mention you are there if she wants to talk or needs help otherwise keep things work related as that will help her feel like something in her life is normal. She will remember you made the offer and may lean on you if needed.

It sounds like your situation was a challenge but you managed it well. It can feel like all the hospital does is dope the patients up and let them go but there is usually more to it than that. It is important, when possible, to research hospitals as some are better than others, the differences can be striking. While the patient is in the hospital that is the time to plan and set up aftercare, your ex should not have been released without a good follow up plan in place. I try and think of the hospital as crisis management for only the worst situations and try to manage everything else with the other resources we have in place.

I wish you and your friend the very best.

I wanted to say that this post helped me a lot. I want to do more for them, but it was helpful to me to know that sometimes it's enough to just be the mom's friend. The boy is out and doing better now.
